concepts.definition: A structure in which the program is in exactly one state at any moment. In DENGE (balance) the control runs; in the other states the motors are off.
concepts.example: When the angle goes past the threshold, the program switches to the DUSTU (fell) state, the LED lights up and the motors are cut.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting that it never leaves the DUSTU state: after picking the robot up you have to restart it.

concepts.definition: If the absolute value of the angle goes past this limit, the robot counts as fallen and the motors are cut.
concepts.example: In the simulation a 40° threshold was chosen; the robot counts as fallen at 45°.
concepts.pitfall: Checking only one direction (aci > threshold): when the robot falls backwards, it is not detected.

concepts.definition: The largest deviation the robot reaches after the push. It shows how hard the control's response is.
concepts.example: In a +200 °/s push, the real largest tilt was measured as 4.96°.
concepts.pitfall: Expecting the robot's report to match the real value exactly: the robot sees the filtered angle, so there are small differences.

concepts.definition: The time it takes after the push for the tilt to drop below the threshold (here 1°) and stay there.
concepts.example: If the tilt last went past 1° 177 ms after the push, the settling time is 177 ms.
concepts.pitfall: Counting the first moment it drops below the threshold as settling: the robot may go past the threshold again.

concepts.definition: KP, KD, KX and KV are specific to the robot. On a real robot you start with small values and tune KP first, then KD, and the outer loop last.
concepts.example: The simulation's KP = 0.15 is either not enough on a real robot or makes it jitter.
concepts.pitfall: Copying the simulation gains onto a real robot.

quiz.prompt: If you do not measure and subtract the gyroscope bias at start-up, what does the balancing robot do?
options: It falls at once, because the error goes to infinity
It stays balanced but carries a permanent tilt error
Only the outer loop stops working
quiz.explanation: The complementary filter limits the build-up of the bias, so the robot does not fall; but the estimate shifts by the bias times the time constant, and the robot stands permanently slightly tilted. In the simulation a 1 °/s bias led to a tilt of about -1.05° and went past the settling threshold.

The angle goes past the 40° threshold and the state is not DUSTU; the first block runs, the state becomes DUSTU and "DUSTU" is printed. The next if goes into the else branch because the state is no longer DENGE: "MOTOR KAPALI" (motor off). Because the state update comes before the control decision, the motors switch off in the same round.

options: The durum != DUSTU condition should be removed
aci > DUSME_ACISI only catches a forward fall; fabs(aci) should be used
durum = DENGE should be written instead of durum = DUSTU
quiz.explanation: The angle of a robot falling backwards is negative, and a negative number is never greater than a positive threshold. fabs(aci) catches both directions. The durum != DUSTU condition prevents printing for no reason; it is correct.

quiz.prompt: In the project, the report is printed if the angle stays below 1° for longer than 1000 ms (ms - sonDisariMs > 1000). If the tilt last went past 1° at 3185 ms, at roughly which ms is the RAPOR line printed? (The loop runs every 5 ms.)
quiz.explanation: The condition is met when ms - 3185 > 1000, that is, when ms goes past 4185; because of the 5 ms rounds, this is about 4186-4190 ms. The settling time reported, however, is not the moment of the report but the time until the tilt last went past 1°: if the push was at 3010 ms, 3185 - 3010 = 175 ms.

quiz.prompt: If you write the KP, KD, KX and KV values that work in the simulation onto a real robot unchanged, what happens?
options: Most likely the robot either does not stay upright or jitters; the gains are tuned again starting small
The same result comes out, because the code is the same
Only KX and KV change; KP and KD stay the same
The robot only reacts a little more slowly
quiz.explanation: The motor power, wheel diameter, mass, height and battery are different; the gains are specific to the robot. The structure of the program (measuring, filter, fixed loop, cascade) stays the same, and the numbers change. The safe way: KP alone first, then KD, and the outer loop last, holding the robot in the air on the first try.
